`pg_easy_replicate` is a CLI orchestrator tool that simplifies the process of setting up logical replication between two PostgreSQL databases. `pg_easy_replicate` also supports switchover. After the source (primary database) is fully replicated, `pg_easy_replicate` puts it into read-only mode and via logical replication flushes all data to the new target database. This ensures zero data loss and minimal downtime for the application. This method can be useful for performing minimal downtime (up to <1min, depending) major version upgrades between a Blue/Green PostgreSQL database setup, load testing and other similar use cases.

Sign-in, staff dashboard, catalog, book detail, and My Loans.

Libro is a full-stack library management system for the library of Aklan State University – College of Computer Studies (ASU-CCS): a Java 25 / Spring Boot REST API with a React and TypeScript web UI (`ui/`), backed by PostgreSQL. It manages physical book copies, user accounts, and loan history, with role-based screens for students, faculty, library assistants, and the librarian. Each catalog record is one physical copy, which keeps loan history accurate per copy (see Domain Decisions).
- **Loans:** students and faculty borrow for 14 days, up to three active loans each; overdue loans block new checkouts. See the Loan Implementation Guide.
- **Security:** stateless HS256 JWT Bearer authentication, BCrypt passwords, per-IP rate limits on login and signup, and a uniform JSON error contract. See the JWT Authentication Design.

- **Web UI:** a React app in `ui/` for sign-in, student signup, catalog and borrowing, My Loans, My Account, and staff dashboards, loan management, inventory, accounts, and audit log. See the Web UI guide.
|Backend|Java 25, Spring Boot 4.1.2 (Web, Data JPA, Security, OAuth2 Resource Server, Validation)|
|Frontend|React 19, TypeScript, Vite, TanStack Query, React Router; Vitest, Playwright, and axe for tests|
|Build and test|Maven, JUnit 5, Mockito, Testcontainers, JaCoCo|
|Delivery|Docker, Docker Compose, Caddy, GitHub Actions, Trivy|

The React UI is a separate app in `ui/` that calls the API with a Bearer token; it has no server-side code of its own. The single-module backend codebase groups `auth`, `book`, `loan`, `user`, `audit`, and `info` by feature, then by layer. Controllers accept and return DTOs; services own business rules, transactions, and entity-to-DTO mapping; repositories own persistence. Shared responses, errors, request IDs, time handling, and OpenAPI configuration live in `global`. Flyway owns the schema, and Hibernate validates it at startup. Architecture Overview shows the request and data flows; its Design Rules section records the package decision.

|`workflow_run` of CI on `main`|The release path. The `image` job runs only when the CI run concluded `success` and was started by a `push`.|
|`workflow_dispatch`|Manual release of the current `main`; the deploy job still needs `production` approval.|

Gate summary, in order: (1) all five CI jobs pass; (2) CI succeeds on a `main` push, which unlocks the CD `image` job; (3) the image passes the Trivy scan before it is pushed; (4) the deploy job requires `DEPLOY_ENABLED=true` plus `production` environment approval; (5) `deploy.sh` passes its health check and smoke test or automatically rolls back. Setup for the environment, secrets, and enable variable is in the Operations Runbook.

`scripts/deploy.sh` already does the deploy step by hand: it backs up the database, starts the new image, runs a smoke test (readiness, login, authenticated read, anonymous rejection), and restarts the previous image if anything fails. Flyway migrations are forward-only, so database recovery uses `scripts/restore.sh`. `backup.sh` and `seed-demo.sh` cover backups and demo data. The pipeline stages, environments, rollback, and monitoring are in CI/CD and DevOps; first deploy, manual update, restore, and automation setup are in the Operations Runbook.

On a provisioned VM, use `scripts/deploy.sh` for a manual release or the runbook's update procedure for a rollback. If a release applied a bad database migration, restore the pre-deploy backup; an application image rollback cannot reverse Flyway migrations.

This is a working proof of concept of the LLM-Wiki pattern, not a finished
product. The core loop — ingest → build/maintain wiki → read → chat with
citations → lint → repair — is fully implemented. Some ideas from the original
- **No web search.** The chat agent answers only from *your* curated local
corpus — it never reaches out to the web, and there's no automatic web→wiki
loop. To bring in an outside source, fetch it yourself (e.g. save the article
as a PDF) and then **ingest it manually** — dropping a file into `sources/`
does nothing on its own. Open the **Ingest** tab and either (a) choose the file in
the upload form and click **Ingest**, or (b) put it in
`WIKI_PATH/sources/` and click **Scan sources/ for changes**, which detects
and ingests anything new or modified. Treat a document from an untrusted origin
the way you'd treat untrusted code: at ingestion its text is turned into wiki
- **Images are ignored by default.** With `[images] ignore = true`, the default,
the images embedded in a document are skipped: not kept, not described. See
- **OCR is off by default.** A scanned / image-only PDF fails with a message until
- **Output is markdown only — no alternate formats.** The wiki
records a full citation/link graph in the database (`document_references`:
which page cites which source, which pages link to which), and the
**Relations** tab draws it. There are no generators for slide
decks (**Marp**) or spatial **canvas** layouts. You read the wiki as linked
- **Ingestion is automated, not a guided conversation.** Karpathy's flow has the
LLM discuss a source with you and write pages under your direction; here you
drop a file and the pipeline extracts → summarises → files it in one shot, with
no mid-ingest review. You steer the wiki *afterwards*: open the resulting page
in the **Read** tab, chat about the document, then save the conversation
as a wiki page with **Save**. The agent only drafts and proposes — you review
the draft in a dialog and the save is your explicit
- **Deleting a source leaves its contribution in the pages it shares.** A page
that cites only the deleted source is deleted, and no link to it is left. A page
that also cites another source is kept, marked stale, and stops citing the deleted
file — but its text and its generated aliases may still hold what that file
contributed, because a page does not record which sentence came from which
source. This applies equally to a deletion from the **Ingest** tab and to a file
removed from `sources/` by hand, which the wiki deletes when you open it. The only
way to remove that text is to rebuild the whole wiki from the remaining sources:
1. In the wiki list, create a new wiki in an empty folder.
2. In its **Ingest** tab, upload the remaining source documents.
3. Copy `wiki_config.toml` from the old wiki: it holds the blacklist and the
Changes made by hand in the old wiki (edited pages, removed topics) are not
carried over. **Rebuild the index** in the **Maintain** tab does not do this: it
rebuilds the search database from the pages as they are.
